text:
David: quick note after RFC sync — i think we should model the control-plane held secret as a 'policy token broker' rather than leaking policy logic into runtimes. broker holds ciphertext + release rules. runtimes must present proof.
Lina: agree. broker is clearer. can we make release adapters pluggable? e.g. hosted uses runtime-attest, dedicated may use corporate-kms proxy, private can be local-operator trigger.
Sam: failure modes we discussed: if attest fails repeatedly in private air-gapped site, customer will want retry/backoff + operator override. default semantics need to be explicit (deny vs degraded).
Kate: suggestion: three-mode fallback: deny, degrade (strip sensitive features), audit-only. map defaults per hosting tier but allow customer override on private.
Maya: implementation note: signed lease + nonces for attestation works, but we should also support a lightweight signed-agent token where hardware attestation isn't available. basically an HSM-backed attestor OR a signed agent keypair.
David: agreed. we should formalize attestor_types: [hwm_attest, agent_signed, kms_release]. include verification steps.
Lina: security: broker should never return full plaintext policy blobs. only short-lived release grants (scoped tokens) which encode permitted actions and TTL. runtime must prove possession for each session or for cached batches.
Sam: caching tradeoffs — cache per (tenant, model, route) with explicit invalidation hooks on rollout. TTLs: keep short (1-5m) for high-sensitivity policies, longer allowed for low-sensitivity. document recommended defaults.
Kate: telemetry: record release_event with fields {policy_id, release_type, evidence_hash, release_cid}. don't log tokens. keep hashes and correlation IDs.
Maya: operator UX: private installs want an offline-trigger flow. propose: control-plane uploads ciphertext; operator runs local tool 'redwood-escrow-unlock --id <policy> --approval <sig>' which calls local KMS and writes a release-record to local audit store. runtime then reads release grant from local controlplane replica. no outbound attestation required.
David: nice. for hosted/dedicated release flow: 1) runtime requests challenge 2) broker issues nonce 3) runtime attests/signs 4) broker validates 5) broker returns short-lived grant token (JWS)
Lina: token format: JWS with fields: sub=tenant, scope=policy_id, exp, rid=request_id, evidence=evidence_hash. signed by broker key. runtime presents in Authorization header to local runtime components.
Sam: rotate signing keys regularly. rotation semantics: publish new jwks, accept old tokens for grace_period (e.g., 10m), and force re-attestation on key rotation for high-sensitivity policies.
Kate: policy DSL: minimal boolean expressions over signals. don't allow loops or external calls. support predicates like in_region("eu"), model_in_allowlist([...]), request_size_lt(1024).
Maya: signals availability matrix: hosted -> full signals (billing, telemetry, identity), dedicated -> reduced (no billing), private -> operator-defined set. document API responses when a signal is missing (return unknown -> conservative decision = deny or warn).
David: decision API idea: POST /policy/check {policy_id, context_signals} -> {decision: allow|deny|degrade, evidence_hash, release_grant?}. runtime-friendly minimal latency.
Lina: perf: attestation adds ~20-80ms. recommend batching tokens per request group and pre-warming grants for hot routes. provide client-side cache with local eviction on model rollouts.
Sam: audit ingestion: release events should emit a compact record to telemetry (no PII) and write append-only audit entries in control-plane DB. ensure ability to export audit for e-discovery.
Kate: emergency operator override: implement a 2-person approval flow (operator A requests, operator B signs) and produce a signed override grant. log and escalate automatically.
Maya: debugging checklist draft: 1) check broker logs for validation failures 2) compare nonce timestamps for skew 3) verify attestor cert chain 4) check jwks for key acceptance 5) inspect evidence_hash mapping for correlation id.
David: update RFC items: - broker primitives & API - attestor types and verification - token format and rotation - caching & invalidation rules - telemetry/audit schema - private offline unlock flow + operator UX - emergency override.
Lina: i'll sketch sequence diagrams + sample config snippet.
```
policy_broker:
  id: pii_block_v2
  release_adapter: agent_signed
  token_ttl_seconds: 300
  enforcement: degrade
  signals_required: [tenant_id, model_id, geo_region]
```
Sam: i'll draft audit schema (compact record layout) and caching behaviour notes.
Kate: i'll add ops playbook + runbooks for private installs. include playbooks for time-skew, cert expiry, and operator override.
Maya: can we add small e2e test harness that simulates hwm_attest vs agent_signed so customers can validate?
David: yes, add e2e harness to RFC repo. next sync: reconvene after drafts next Tues.
